artifact.scope: Teaching and conditional V&V planning only, tracing proposed REQ01 and REQ02 from ProblemBrief r1 and the conditional PrototypePlan r1. Verification addresses requirement conformity; validation addresses suitability for intended use. No approved requirements baseline, execution, performance result or acceptance is established. All activities depend on resolving criteria, configuration and resources before execution. The lunar case supplies no clamp parameters or performance proof.

conditions.text: The supplied task requests a bench clamp that holds a workpiece without damage.
REQ01 retention and REQ02 damage prevention remain proposed in ProblemBrief r1. Their hardness remains unknown; no approved technical baseline is supplied.
Customer loads, material, geometry, allowable movement, damage criterion, intended operator and operating environment are unknown.

Prototype configuration, representative workpieces, equipment, observation capability, personnel, sampling rationale and requirement confirmation authority are unknown. M01 and M02 remain unresolved concepts.

Proposed planning rule: establish criteria and record configuration before execution; retain raw records, deviations and anomalies against requirement IDs and configuration versions. Changes require impact review and identification of affected activities before evidence is reused.
The supplied lunar-sampling excerpt concerns a different environment and has unestablished transferability. Its provenance does not establish clamp performance or customer requirements.

matrix.criterion: Proposed, not executable yet: compare recorded workpiece movement with an allowable limit established before execution, under defined loads, directions and holding duration. Limits, observation uncertainty, repetitions and decision rules are unresolved. Missing or inadequate observations must leave conformity unverified.
matrix.configuration: Conditional functional prototype from PrototypePlan r1; route, version and construction remain undefined. Before execution, record contact geometry, actuation, support attachment, workpiece material and geometry, loading arrangement, environment, measurement equipment and procedure version. Establish controlled conditions and stopping rules first.

matrix.criterion: Proposed, not executable yet: compare workpiece condition before engagement and after holding and release against a predeclared damage definition and limits. Establish an inspection method capable of detecting the relevant changes and account for observation uncertainty and handling effects. No visible change alone cannot establish absence of relevant damage.
matrix.configuration: Use a documented prototype and workpiece configuration linked to the retention activity where appropriate. Record initial surface condition, contact arrangement, restraint input, loading history, release sequence, inspection method and equipment. Configuration and detection capability remain unknown.

matrix.criterion: Proposed: a representative intended operator completes the defined engagement, holding and intentional-release task in a representative use setting, with task success and unacceptable intervention defined beforehand. Operator, task and success conditions are unknown. Demonstration observations do not substitute for quantitative retention verification.
matrix.configuration: Intended-use scenario, operator characteristics, bench interface and representative prototype remain undefined. Record differences from intended use and all assistance or intervention. Physical demonstration remains blocked until conditions and controls are established.

matrix.criterion: Proposed: assess whether the workpiece remains suitable for its defined subsequent use after the complete clamping task, using stakeholder-defined suitability criteria and an adequate assessment method. Intended subsequent use and criteria are unknown. User satisfaction cannot replace damage verification.
matrix.configuration: May share the intended-use activity with REQ01 validation, but retain a separate suitability judgment and traceable workpiece assessment. Record operator, task, prototype, workpiece, environment and assessment configuration; all remain to be defined.

validation_questions: Who uses the clamp, for which operation, in which bench environment, and what defines successful task completion?
Which workpiece materials, finishes, geometries and variations must be represented?
What loads, directions, durations and allowable movements define retention?
What changes constitute damage, and what subsequent workpiece use must remain possible?
Who can confirm requirements and criteria, determine hardness and authorize changes?
Which prototype route, configuration, resources and observation capabilities can represent the intended conditions?
Which abnormal scenarios, including slip, input loss and incomplete release, require separate controlled activities?
What sampling, uncertainty and configuration limitations must accompany any later findings?
